messages.subject: different counts with two annotation files
messages.subject_clean: different counts with two annotation files
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I have (human) total RNA-seq data. Following alignment with STAR I performed counting using the featureCounts function of Rsubread and the annotation file Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.96.gtf. For the long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) I also performed counting using the annotation file gencode.v30.long_noncoding_RNAs.gtf. Comparing counts for all lncRNAs from both annotation files, to my surprise they are not the same, they are the same for some lncRNAs but not for other lncRNAs. I checked some of the lncRNAs for which the counts are different and their genomic start and end positions are exactly the same in both annotation files. I do not understand why I get different counts. Can anyone explain this to me? The featureCounts code is below.
Thanks, Ina

  counts_5466_190402B6.out <- featureCounts(files=mapped.flist,
     annot.inbuilt="hg38", chrAliases=NULL,

    # use ensembl GTF file
    #annot.ext="/home/inah/RefGTF_38_96/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.96.gtf",
    annot.ext="/home/inah/RefGTF_38_96/gencode.v30.long_noncoding_RNAs.gtf",
    isGTFAnnotationFile=TRUE,
    GTF.featureType="exon", GTF.attrType="gene_id", useMetaFeatures=TRUE,
    #GTF.featureType="exon", GTF.attrType="exon_id", useMetaFeatures=TRUE,

    # overlap between reads and features
    allowMultiOverlap=TRUE,
    minOverlap=1,
    largestOverlap=TRUE,

    # multi-mapping reads
    countMultiMappingReads=FALSE,
    fraction=FALSE,

    # strandness
    strandSpecific=2,    # 0=unstranded, 1=stranded, 2=reversely stranded

    # read filtering
    minMQS=0,

    # parameters specific to paired end reads
    isPairedEnd=TRUE,
    requireBothEndsMapped=FALSE,
    checkFragLength=FALSE,
    minFragLength=50,
    maxFragLength=600,
    countChimericFragments=TRUE,
    autosort=TRUE,

    # number of CPUs
    nthreads=1 )

messages.body_plain:
I noticed that you set " largestOverlap = TRUE ". This made the assignment of reads to the lncRNA regions not only depend on the lncRNA annotations themselves, but also depend on other annotations (eg actual exons of genes) in your GTF files.

Say, a read has 30 bases overlapping with a lncRNA, and it has 40 bases overlapping with an exon in the Ensembl GTF file, then this read is uniquely assigned to the exon but not the lncRNA when featureCounts runs on the Ensembl GTF file. On the other hand, the Gencode GTF file doesn't include this exon, hence this read is assigned to the lncRNA when featureCounts runs on the Gencode GTF file.

messages.body_plain: I think setting largestOverlap = TRUE is good for distinguishing the lncRNA reads from the other reads in the total RNA-seq data. If a read has longer overlapping with an actual exon, it is much unlikely from a lncRNA and this can reduce the noise in the counts to the lncRNA regions. To that end, a GTF file mixing lncRNA and exons (like the Ensembl GTF file) is better for the analysis.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am analyzing human total RNA-seq data (from Nova-seq) on a linux cluster. Running Rsubread function featureCounts on 477 alignment files (from STAR) gives me this distribution for the proportion of successfully assigned fragments:
Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.
 0.00   49.85   57.80   53.56   63.95   72.20
This is worse than what I am used to seeing (with mRNA data).
I am loading R-bundle-Bioconductor/3.7-foss-2018b-R-3.5.1 which is the latest version currently available (easybuild). Below is sessionInfo():

So I am using a dated version of Rsubread, which I assume is the reason why I am getting the warning:

||             reporting of multi-mapping read pairs).                        ||

Does anyone think that my use of the dated version of Rsubread could be causing the relatively low proportions of successfully assigned fragments?

Thanks, Ina

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ina,

First of all, the WARNING message of "same pair were found not adjacent to each other" is always reported when featureCounts runs on SAM/BAM files from STAR (and a few other aligners). The counting results should be all correct even this WARNING message is shown. FeatureCounts is very unlikely to generate incorrect counts -- when something seems wrong, the program terminates and no values are returned from the function.

The version of Rsubread that you are using shouldn't be the problem. The latest version is 1.34.1, but the behaviour of featureCounts hasn't changed, only faster and with more options / functionality.

>From the information you provided, it is very hard to figure out what caused, as you said, the low assignment proportions. For example, what is the old analytic pipeline that you used to have a higher assignment proportion, and what is the setting of the old experiments, etc.

Cheers,
Yang
